title: Crypto & Identity Gating PRD — test scenarios, scope clarifications, and rollout checklist
creator: Connor Nguyen
description: PRD to finalize security controls for Private deployments: SSO/SAML & OIDC integrations, RBAC model & enforcement, audit log export/retention guarantees, and customer-managed key (CMEK/HSM) requirements. Includes clarified scope, acceptance criteria, test scenarios, and a rollout/checklist for phased delivery.
background: Customers deploying Redwood Private have requested enterprise-grade identity and keying controls. Past audits highlighted ambiguous RBAC coverage and gaps in tamper-evident audit exports. This PRD consolidates decisions from compliance reviews and engineering feasibility work to produce testable acceptance criteria and a safe rollout plan.
goals: Ship SAML and OIDC SSO integrations with SCIM-based provisioning and IdP-initiated login support
Deliver RBAC primitives mapped to product capabilities (Owner/Admin/Developer/Viewer) and enforce via service-side policy checks
Provide auditable, exportable, tamper-evident audit logs for all identity, permission, and keying events
Enable customer-managed keys (CMEK) via KMS/HSM integrations with rotation and key revocation workflows
Define precise acceptance criteria and test scenarios so QA and security can sign off
non_goals: Implementing a full enterprise identity provider (we integrate with 3rd-party IdPs only)
Building custom HSM hardware — we rely on cloud HSM/KMS integrations and documented KMIP-compatible flows
Multi-tenant per-customer dedicated HSM appliances in the initial rollout (considered for future phase)
requirements: SSO: Support SAML 2.0 SP-initiated and IdP-initiated flows; OIDC authorization code flow with PKCE as optional; configurable assertion mappings for email, groups, and external_id
SCIM: Provide SCIM v2 endpoints for provisioning/deprovisioning with a minimum of create/update/delete for users and group membership
RBAC: Role model with at least four roles (Owner, Admin, Developer, Readonly); enforce role checks on all Console and API actions; audit all role changes

Audit logs: Append-only audit store with immutable export to customer S3 or secure cloud storage; include fields for actor, action, resource, timestamp, request_id, and raw_event; retention configurable per customer (30/90/365 days)

KMS/HSM: Support customer-managed keys via KMS APIs (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, GCP CMEK) and HSM-backed key wrapping; support key rotation, rewrap, and emergency key revocation with documented failover behavior
Key access controls: KMS key policies and HSM ACLs must be honored; Redwood must never store customer plaintext key material; all uses of CMEK must be logged in audit events
Operational: Console UI for SSO and KMS onboarding, CLI flags for private deploy manifests, and API endpoints for programmatic configuration
Security controls: MFA enforcement via IdP where supported; session length configurable; admin action confirmation step for destructive actions (eg. key revoke, permission grant to Owner)
scope_changes: Scope clarified: initial delivery will include SAML + OIDC and SCIM for provisioning. Additional IdP-specific adapters (Okta advanced profile transforms) deferred to append-only follow-ups.
Decision: HSM support limited to cloud-hosted HSM/KMS integrations (no on-prem KMIP server in phase 1). KMIP adapter scoped for Phase 2 based on partner demand.
Change: Audit retention UI will support preset buckets (30/90/365) at GA; fully custom retention policies scheduled post-GA.
Clarification: Role hierarchy will be flat for GA (no inheritence rules); fine-grained grants (resource-scoped permissions) will be delivered as 'alpha' to select customers
acceptance_criteria: Identity: A test IdP (SAML) can successfully authenticate a user and a SCIM-provisioned group is reflected in Console and via API within 60s
RBAC enforcement: For each role, an automated test asserts allowed and denied API calls with pass/fail matrix (test coverage >= 95% for listed actions)
Audit export: A simulated admin action produces an audit event persisted in append-only store and exported to a customer S3 location within 2 minutes; exported logs are verifiable (SHA256 manifest)

CMEK: Customer can register a KMS key, and the system uses the key to encrypt at-rest secrets; rotating the key triggers rewrap and a logged event; revoking key access causes controlled failover to a locked state and an alert to oncall
Security review: External security team runs checklist and marks all items green; any remaining open items are tracked with remediation tickets before GA
Documentation: Onboarding guide, API reference, and runbook published with step-by-step SSO/KMS setup and troubleshooting
Performance: Enabling audit export and CMEK adds no more than 10% median latency to token issuance paths under a standard private-deploy load profile
test_scenarios: Happy path: IdP SAML login -> SCIM provisioned user -> assign Developer role -> call generation API -> verify audit event
Provisioning failure: SCIM 400 responses are surfaced to admin UI with retry guidance and idempotent protection (tests assert safe retry)
Key rotation: Register test KMS key, write sample secrets, rotate key via KMS API, verify secrets rewrap and re-encryption logs emitted
Partial outage: Simulate KMS API 503; system transitions to 'service degraded' with restricted write operations and alerts to SRE
RBAC regression: Run negative tests where Developer attempts Owner-only actions; ensure action blocked and a security-audit event created
Audit export tamper check: Exported log bundle must include a manifest; manipulation of export bundle is detected by manifest mismatch test
rollout_checklist: 0: Merge gated PRs and complete dependency ENG tickets (ENG-1842)
1: Deploy to internal canary private cluster with a seeded IdP and CMEK test keys; smoke tests green
2: Run automated RBAC matrix tests and audit export tests against canary cluster
3: Invite 2 pilot customers with non-production data; collect feedback for 2 weeks
4: Security and legal sign-off obtained (explicit checklist items cleared)
5: Gradual rollout: 10% customers -> 30% -> 100% over two weeks, with SLO monitoring: auth_success_rate, audit_export_latency, key_op_error_rate
6: Post-rollout review and retrospective; record any scope adjustments as follow-up PM tickets

notes: Risk: Key revocation UX may cause customer confusion; mitigation: explicit pre-revoke dry-run and confirmation modal
Risk: SCIM provisioning can be slow for large orgs; mitigation: asynchronous sync with clear admin status and bulk ops
Monitoring: Add SLO dashboards for auth latency, audit-export success rate, and CMEK key-op latency
Follow-ups: Phase 2 will include KMIP, per-resource grants, and extended custom retention policies
